title: The HMX Story
intro: HMX is a small statically typed language by Himanshu Kumar that transpiles to C and ships a native binary — plus a browser playground that runs the whole compiler client-side. This is how it started, where it is now, and what still stands between it and production.

chapters.title: How it started
chapters.body: A deliberately small compiler: a Flex lexer, a Bison parser, a C++ AST / type-resolver / code generator, and gcc as the backend.

entries.title: A minimal transpiler
entries.detail: let declarations, print, loop(count), zero-arg functions, arithmetic, and line comments — the whole pipeline from a .hmx source file to a native binary.

entries.title: Hello-world capable (Phases 1–8)
entries.detail: Block comments, comparisons, boolean logic, if/else, assignment, typed function parameters and returns, and function calls with recursion. The language could finally write real programs.

chapters.title: How it's going
chapters.body: From hello-world to a packaged, tested, distributed compiler with a byte-identical browser backend.

entries.title: Strings, loops, and arrays
entries.detail: text + text concatenation, the full loop family (loop/while/for/do-while/foreach), growable and nested arrays, and the array built-ins (push, pop, sort, slice, concat, index_of, contains).

entries.title: Tuples, destructuring, and text ops
entries.detail: Multiple return values via tuples, nested destructuring with ...rest, byte-level text indexing, ord/chr/split, tostr/parse_int/parse_decimal, input(), and variadic print.

entries.title: First-class functions
entries.detail: Function types, higher-order calls, closures with transitive captures, anonymous lambdas and currying via partial application, and non-local break/continue.

entries.title: Modules and the web playground
entries.detail: Cross-file use modules with top-level state and cycle detection; Unicode identifiers; and a full native-parity compiler ported to TypeScript, so HMX runs entirely in the browser.

entries.title: Memory: a reference-counted runtime (M15)
entries.detail: text, arrays, and closure environments are reference-counted, with copy-on-write views; locals own and parameters borrow. Gated under AddressSanitizer + LeakSanitizer and Valgrind.

entries.title: Structures: structs, enums, aliases (M16)
entries.detail: Nominal value-type structs, int-backed enums with switch support, and transparent type aliases — plus a heap-use-after-free found and fixed by the new ownership matrix.

entries.title: CLI hardening, soundness, distribution (M9–M14)
entries.detail: Bare hmx file.hmx runs, help/version, hmx new, runtime crash reporting, lexer overflow checks, byte arithmetic, global identifier mangling, and module top-level state.

entries.title: Shipped on every channel we can reach (v0.10.0)
entries.detail: Signed releases with .deb, tar.gz and zip; install.sh and install.ps1; a Homebrew formula, a Scoop bucket, a winget manifest (PR open), an AUR PKGBUILD, and a signed opt-in pacman repository. Commits are GPG-signed and verified.

entries.title: A real home on the web
entries.detail: Install, license, 404 and story pages added to the playground, with the routing and packaging gates that keep them honest.

entries.title: Generics, part one: generic functions (M17.1)
entries.detail: Type parameters on functions — fn identity[T](x: T) -> T — inferred at each call site and monomorphized into its own specialization, with no constraints. Native and web stay byte-identical, and a reflective clone that overflowed on the nonlocal-exit back-pointer was replaced by a faithful node-by-node port.

chapters.title: What's left until production level
chapters.body: The gap between a great small language and a language a team would bet on. Grouped by pillar; the sequencing lives in PRODUCTION.md.

entries.title: Correctness, safety, and trust
entries.detail: Checked runtime integer overflow; recoverable errors instead of bare exit(1); a cycle-collection decision before generics; UBSan and TSan in CI; a front-end fuzz target and coverage; diagnosable allocation failures.

entries.title: Language completeness
entries.detail: Generics (M17); Option/Result with try/?/defer (M18); a fixed-width numeric tower with checked arithmetic (M19); UTF-8 string semantics; real pattern matching; traits/interfaces; visibility and namespaces; references/ownership; methods, defer/RAII and assert; and the handful of grammar bugs.

entries.title: A standard library
entries.detail: There is no standard library today: file and OS I/O, math, HashMap/Set, text utilities, JSON/CSV, regex, dates, and (stretch) networking.

entries.title: Tooling and developer experience
entries.detail: A debugger story (-g DWARF, stack traces), a REPL, a formatter, an LSP, a package manager with a manifest and lockfile, a test runner, a doc generator, hmx check, and real warnings with multi-error diagnostics.

entries.title: Compiler and backend
entries.detail: An IR layer (M26), a second backend (bytecode VM / LLVM), HMX-level optimization, more prebuilt targets, a self-contained toolchain, and clang coverage in CI.

entries.title: Interop
entries.detail: A C FFI so HMX can call OpenSSL, libcurl, SQLite, zlib and friends; packaged C libraries; and an ABI-stability statement.

entries.title: Ecosystem and governance
entries.detail: CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT and SECURITY files; an RFC and deprecation policy; a tutorial/book and a standard-library reference; and published benchmarks.

entries.title: QA and performance
entries.detail: A benchmark suite with a performance-regression gate, property and differential testing beyond web parity, a UBSan/TSan matrix, and golden diagnostics.
